facts.statement: Kunpengornis is an extinct genus of euornithean birds.
facts.quote: Kunpengornis (meaning "Kunpeng bird") is an extinct genus of euornithean birds

facts.statement: Fish bones found in its abdominal cavity indicate that Kunpengornis was a fish-eater.
facts.quote: Fish bones preserved in the abdominal cavity indicate that Kunpengornis was piscivorous.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered by a farmer in the Jiufotang Formation.
facts.quote: The Kunpengornis holotype specimen, AGB 15483, was discovered by a farmer in outcrops of the Jiufotang Formation

facts.statement: The farmer who found the fossil donated it to the Anhui Geological Museum in 2023.
facts.quote: who donated it to Anhui Geological Museum in 2023 to be researched, where it is now accessioned.

facts.statement: The fossil was found near Lamadong in Jianchang County, Liaoning Province, China.
facts.quote: It was found near Lamadong in Jianchang County of Liaoning Province, China.

facts.statement: The genus name combines the mythical Chinese Kunpeng with the Greek word for bird.
facts.quote: The generic name, Kunpengornis, combines a reference to the mythical Chinese Kunpeng—known for its ability to transform into either a fish or a giant bird—with the Greek ornis, meaning "bird".

facts.statement: The species name anhuimusei honors the Anhui Geological Museum which holds the holotype.
facts.quote: The specific name, anhuimusei, references the Anhui Geological Museum, which houses the holotype.

facts.statement: Kunpengornis lived during the Early Cretaceous (Aptian age) in Liaoning Province, China.
facts.quote: Kunpengornis (meaning "Kunpeng bird") is an extinct genus of euornithean birds known from the Early Cretaceous (Aptian age) Jiufotang Formation of Liaoning Province, China.

facts.statement: Kunpengornis lived between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Kunpengornis is the genus name for this extinct bird.
The only known species is Kunpengornis anhuimusei.
The genus was established by Huang et al. in 2026.
Phylogenetic analyses place Kunpengornis within Euornithes as the sister taxon to Piscivoravis.
facts.quote: In their phylogenetic analyses, Huang et al. (2026) recovered Kunpengornis as a member of the Euornithes, as the sister taxon to Piscivoravis.

facts.statement: The clade containing Kunpengornis diverged after the Yanornithidae but before the Gansuidae and Ornithuromorpha.
facts.quote: In turn, this clade was found to diverge after the Yanornithidae, but before the Gansuidae and Ornithuromorpha.

facts.statement: Euornithes is the parent group of Kunpengornis.
Kunpengornis is classified under the class Reptilia.
